dish: Seifuku awamori tasting (and the Seifuku Coole liqueur)
n: Seifuku Shuzō awamori distillery, Ishigaki (請福酒造)
w: Ishigaki awamori maker founded in 1949, with a direct shop where the whole Seifuku range can be tasted and free ~15-minute factory tours at set times, no booking needed.

n: Yaesen Shuzō awamori distillery, Ishigaki (八重泉酒造)
w: Founded in 1955; the factory shop shows a 15-minute film of the distilling process and runs a tasting counter with shop-only bottles. Three Yaesen awamori won awards at a UK spirits competition (Ryukyu Shimpo).

dish: Omoto awamori, distilled over a direct-fire earthen kiln
n: Takamine Shuzōsho awamori distillery, Kabira (高嶺酒造所)
w: Small distillery beside Kabira Park making 'Omoto' awamori by hand — one of the few still using direct-fire (jika-bi) distillation; the process is visible through glass and tastings are offered.

dish: Ishigaki-gyū A4/A5 yakiniku, rare cuts from whole-animal purchase
n: Yakiniku Takesan-tei, Ishigaki (焼肉 たけさん亭)
w: Ishigaki-beef yakiniku whose owner holds cattle-auction buying rights and buys whole A4–A5 animals, so rarer cuts appear on the menu. Dinner only (closed Tue).

dish: Ishigaki-gyū yakiniku from the family's own herd
n: Yakiniku Kingyū, Ishigaki (焼肉 金牛)
w: Run by an Ishigaki family that has raised wagyu on the island for over 120 years; serves only its own Ishigaki beef, raised ~30 months and aged. Dinner only (closed Thu).

dish: Tarama awamori aged in a cave storehouse (kusu)
w: Maker of the long-selling 'Taragawa' awamori, brewed with spring water; free 40-minute tours of the plant and its cave storehouse run three times a day (closed Sun).

n: Yukishio Museum, Miyako (雪塩ミュージアム)
w: Showroom of the 'Yukishio' salt works, which makes powder-fine salt from limestone-filtered underground seawater; free guided looks at the production line, and the shop's Yukishio soft-serve is the draw.

dish: Gyūniku soba — stir-fried peppered beef on Okinawa soba
w: Yanbaru noodle shop founded in 1972, on the way to Hiji Falls and Mt Yonaha; its signature gyūniku soba piles pepper-fried beef and bean sprouts on thin noodles, and weekend queues are the norm. Closes when the broth runs out.

dish: Yanbaru shima-buta (agu-line island pork) grilled on a shichirin, incl. pork tongue & offal
n: Shima-buta Shichirin-yaki Manmi, Motobu (島豚七輪焼 満味)
w: Reservation-essential grill house for Yanbaru island pork descended from agu: cuts and offal grilled over individual charcoal shichirin, with rare pork tongue and a horumon fried rice to finish. Dinner only (closed Sun–Mon).
